title: I’m building a Duck Hunt-inspired game where the backgrounds fight back
author: I-want-to-say
selftext:
I’m building Pluck Em! mostly solo, and lately I’ve been overhauling its locations so they’re more than just different scenery.

I’ve been adding animations, gameplay gimmicks and a bunch of little surprises to make each location feel different (but I’m deliberately trying not to show too much, because discovering them is part of the fun).

Here’s a quick look at some of the new versions.

There’s a playable demo on Steam if you want to see what else is hiding in the Farm location.

replies.body: Yes. A few. E.g. Claude

replies.author: RevenueChemical6910
replies.body:
ah I meant the MCP of a graphics provider from within Claude, Claude's image-gen sucks

Do you use a website to generate graphics or type out the assets you need in a prompt, then Claude has an MCP connector to some online platform (fal.ai for instance)

replies.author: I-want-to-say
replies.body: Oh, this is a combination af few pipelines. I use Autosprite, Runway, Chat GPT, Moonlake, end few more less popular. But all.of them requires manual adjustments to work properly in game. AI isn't that accurate in 2D animated graphics yet. So yeah i generate assets outside Claude and import them manually, then use claude for coding, etc.

comments.author: New-Association5536
comments.body: Man, gaming is really just hitting the slop flood stage thanks to AI. All these games are just knock offs of games already released over the last few decades without any new creativity or forward movement.

replies.author: I-want-to-say
replies.body:
That’s pretty much the entire entertainment industry in a nutshell. But the reuse you’re talking about existed waaaay before AI became a thing.
Every creator takes bits and pieces from things they’ve enjoyed (games, movies, books, whatever) and mixes them together with their own ideas and taste.
Give the demo a try. Check what my take on “knocking off a legend” actually looks like.

comments.author: Key-End-2996
comments.body: What's your workflow for graphics? They look great and are consistent throughout the scene and game

replies.author: I-want-to-say
replies.body: That's the most time consuming part I'm affraid. Long story short: Create FInal composition and divide it into layers -> animate layers with Runway -> extract frame by frame --> clean it up (remove background, ad/remove bad  pixels, spills form bachround,etc. - this is manual work) - put png into engine and create flipbooks and done. A lot of manual work,
